title: Light-Years: Measuring the Unmeasurable
objective: After this level you can explain what a light-year measures and how far the nearest star is.
summary: A light-year is a distance: about 9.46 trillion km. The nearest star after the Sun, Proxima Centauri, is about 4.2 light-years away.

cards.headline: A light-year sounds like a unit of time. It isn't.
cards.body: It has 'year' right there in the name, so it's a fair guess. But a light-year is a ruler, not a clock.

cards.headline: Distance, measured in light
cards.body: A light-year is how far light travels in one year: about 9.46 trillion kilometers. So it's a distance, the way a mile is. Kilometers are great for a road trip. Out among the stars they pile up into numbers nobody can read, so astronomers switched to a bigger ruler.

cards.headline: Why measure space in light?
cards.body: Light is the fastest thing there is, which makes it a handy measuring tape. It crosses from the Moon to Earth in just over a second. From the Sun, it takes about 8 minutes (Level 1's slightly late Sun). So the Moon is about one light-second away and the Sun about 8 light-minutes. Past the Sun, even light needs years, and the ruler grows to match.

cards.fact: The closest star after the Sun is Proxima Centauri, about 4.2 light-years away.
cards.context: So its light takes about 4.2 years to reach us. Moon: a second. Sun: 8 minutes. Next star: more than four years. And that's the closest one; every other star is even farther. Proxima is our next-door neighbor. The street is just very, very long.

options.label: Time
options.rationale: It's a common mix-up, but it's a distance.

options.label: Speed
options.rationale: Light's speed is fixed; this is how far it goes in a year.

questions.explanation: A light-year is the distance light travels in one year.

questions.prompt: Proxima Centauri is about 4.2 light-years away. What does that mean?

options.label: It's 4.2 years old
options.rationale: A light-year measures distance, not age.

options.label: A spacecraft could reach it in 4.2 years
options.rationale: Our fastest probes would take thousands of years.

options.label: Its light takes about 4.2 years to reach us
It's 4.2 times farther than the Sun
options.rationale: It's hundreds of thousands of times farther.

questions.explanation: A light-year is how far light goes in a year, so light from Proxima Centauri left it about 4.2 years before you see it.

questions.prompt: From Level 1: about how long does sunlight take to reach Earth?

options.label: About 4.2 years
options.rationale: That's roughly the distance to Proxima Centauri.

questions.explanation: Sunlight takes about 8 minutes to reach Earth, so the Sun is about 8 light-minutes away.
